key: When Indra and the Angirases desired it, Sarama found provision for her offspring.
s: Praising Indra, through whom the Angirases found the cattle, the hymn turns to the search; Sāyaṇa, on 1.62.3, reads it through the tale of Sarama, the gods’ hound, sent after the cows the Paṇis stole once Indra promised their milk to her young.
src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 1.62.3, sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 400586 (2024)

opened.locator: commentary on 1.62.3 (the ākhyāna before the word-by-word gloss); 1.62.2 and 1.62.4 read for context
translation of 1.62.3 and note b (Saramā’s condition that the milk go to her young)

evidence.words: अत्रेदमाख्यानम् । सरमा नाम देवशुनी । पणिभिर्गोष्वपहृतासु तद्गवेषणाय तां सरमामिन्द्रः प्रहैषीत्। यथा लोके व्याधो वनान्तर्गतमृगान्वेषणाय श्वानं विसृजति तद्वत् । सा च सरमा एवमवोचत्। हे इन्द्र अस्मदीयाय शिशवे तद्गोसंबन्धि क्षीराद्यन्नं यदि प्रयच्छसि तर्हि गमिष्यामीति । स तथेत्यब्रवीत्
evidence.gloss: Here is the story. Saramā is the name of the gods’ bitch. When the cows had been carried off by the Paṇis, Indra sent Saramā to search for them, as in the world a hunter lets loose a dog to track the deer in the forest. And Saramā said: Indra, if you give my young one food from those cows, milk and the like, then I will go. He said: so be it.

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, ref 1.62.3, at [61,3]), the first sentence of the verse. Sāyaṇa opens his comment on 1.62.3 with the ākhyāna: Saramā the devaśunī, sent by Indra after the cows the Paṇis carried off, agrees to go on condition that the cows’ milk and food go to her young, and Indra consents; he then glosses tanayāya dhāsim as food for her own son. Every element of the reading (gods’ hound, Paṇis, sent after the cows, milk promised to her young) is in these words; Wilson’s note b agrees. Plain sense: 1.62.2 praises Indra through whom the Angirases found the cattle, and 1.62.3 tells of the finding; ‘search’ matches Griffith’s ‘knowing well the places, found the cattle’; no four words of the key; faithful. Revision 400586 is dated 2024-02-09 by the Wikisource API. Yāska: no verse of this hymn in Sarup’s list. Evidence re-found by machine in the packet. entry-check ok.
